ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the middle of the figure there is a horizontal “pressure belt”; above it is marked “wind belt 1,” with the arrow roughly slanting toward the upper left; below the pressure belt is marked “wind belt 2,” with the arrow roughly pointing from the upper left to the lower right. Then reason: wind belt 2 is located on the south side of this pressure belt, and according to the global distribution of pressure belts and wind belts, it can be judged to be the prevailing westerlies belt in the Southern Hemisphere. The prevailing westerlies bring moist air currents from the ocean for a long time, causing regions affected by them to form a temperate maritime climate that is mild and humid throughout the year. A typical region in the Southern Hemisphere affected by this wind belt and mild and humid throughout the year is New Zealand.
